name: Toyota Tacoma
engine: 3.5L V6 (2GR-FKS), 278 hp — 2.7L naturally-aspirated I4 (2TR-FE), 159 hp base
drivetrain: RWD or part-time 4WD (available locking rear diff and Crawl Control on TRD Off-Road/Pro)
transmission: 6-speed automatic · 6-speed manual (available on V6 TRD Sport/Off-Road/Pro)
reliability: 8/10 — the third-gen Tacoma has a genuinely durable drivetrain and the best resale value of any midsize truck, but it is not without gripes. The 3.5L V6 and 6-speed automatic hold up well, though the transmission can lug and 'hunt' at low rpm in the name of economy (many owners just drive it in a lower gear or ECT mode). The ride is trucky and bouncy on the rear leaf springs, and it uses rear drum brakes. Early 2016–2017 cars saw some rear-differential and driveline vibration complaints. Buy a well-kept one and it will run for a very long time.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate · Maintenance ~$500/yr · Fuel economy is only average for the class · Best-in-class resale — Tacomas are famously expensive to buy used because they hold value so well
popular_mods: All-terrain tires and a mild lift/leveling kit — the classic first upgrades
Better rear suspension (add-a-leaf or aftermarket leaf pack) to settle the bouncy unladen ride
Skid plates, sliders, and a bed rack or camper setup for overlanding
A tune/exhaust does little on the naturally-aspirated V6 — spend on tires and suspension instead
Honest take: the Tacoma is bought for durability and resale, not speed — the manual V6 TRD is the enthusiast pick; everything else is about capability and protection
oil_interval: Per the Maintenance Minder (~5,000–7,500 miles; many owners run 5,000)

generations.2nd Gen (2005–2015 US): The truck that cemented the Tacoma's reputation — 2.7L four or a 4.0L V6, tough and simple. Frame-rust recalls affected some early trucks (Toyota bought many back).
generations.3rd Gen (2016–2023 US): A more modern redesign — 3.5L V6 (278 hp) or 2.7L four, 6-speed automatic or manual, and serious TRD Off-Road/Pro hardware. Best resale in the class, if trucky to drive.
generations.4th Gen (2024+ US): A ground-up redesign on the TNGA-F platform with turbocharged four-cylinder power (including an i-FORCE MAX hybrid) and an 8-speed automatic — much stronger and more modern; a clean third-gen is the proven value.

common_issues: 6-speed automatic lugging/'hunting' at low rpm for economy — annoying but not a failure; ECT mode or manual shifting helps
Bouncy, firm rear leaf-spring ride when the bed is empty — the most common comfort complaint
Rear drum brakes and only-average fuel economy for the class
Some 2016–2017 driveline/rear-differential vibration and a leaky rear-diff pinion seal reported
Frame rust in heavy road-salt regions on older trucks — inspect the frame on Northern examples
maintenance_tips: Change the 0W-20 oil on time and keep the 6-speed automatic fluid fresh despite 'lifetime' claims
Service the transfer case and differential fluids on schedule, especially if you tow or wheel it
Inspect the frame and rear differential for rust and leaks, particularly in salt-belt states
Have any open recalls confirmed closed by VIN before buying
On the manual, do the clutch hydraulic fluid; the clutch itself is long-lived if not abused
